text: I check the time after playing an exciting mahjong game and realize it's almost time to leave home. I'm to meet Ciri outside the Raven hideout at the time we agreed upon with Soumu yesterday.

To my surprise, when I open my living room door, I see two people standing on the left and right side of my door, looking at each other. They are Nadeshiko, who I haven't seen for many days, and Ciri, who I was just with yesterday.
The silence between them inexplicably makes it seem much colder outside the door than inside. It also makes me feel guilty for some reason even though I hadn't done anything.
Since it looks like neither of them intends to speak first, I force myself to break the deadlock.
player
{character:player}Um... Why are you both outside my door?
Nadeshiko
{character:Nadeshiko}Are you asking me? Or are you...
{character:player}Ahahaha... I'm asking both of you.
{character:Nadeshiko}I've made some modifications to my beloved motorcycle and have come to take you out for a ride so you can experience it.
I turn and look at Ciri inquisitively. She glances sideways at me and speaks nonchalantly.
Ciri
{character:Ciri}I've come to take you to the agreed meeting place.
{character:Nadeshiko}The agreed meeting place...?

I can understand that Ciri wouldn't want to tell Nadeshiko about Raven since they don't really know each other, but it's obvious that Nadeshiko has misunderstood the meaning of "the agreed meeting place."
She looks all over me with a strange expression and then looks at Ciri standing opposite to her.
{character:Nadeshiko}No wonder those juniors at Asaha High School keep saying they can't get hold of you recently. So you've been busy dating.
Juniors... Is she referring to Nana Shiraishi?! It must be because I haven't been replying her text messages! She is spreading rumors about me and defaming and slandering me!
{character:player}Nadeshiko, listen to me. It's not what you think.

Yikes! I only realize how terrible this line sounds after I say it, but I don't have a choice. If I don't clarify this now, I'm afraid that everyone in Asaha High School will know about it by tomorrow.
{character:Nadeshiko}Oh, then I'll treat it as a misunderstanding. In that case, will you come with me for a ride or...?
After hearing what Nadeshiko says, Ciri also folds her arms and looks at me with raised eyebrows. She doesn't say anything, but she is emitting intense pressure.

Is this the so-called "battlefield of love" that I've only heard rumors about? Is this my chance to be the protagonist for free? If that's the case, there should be two options in front of me right now...
Wait a minute! I shouldn't be thinking about that right now. This isn't a galgame!
Ciri and I aren't going out on a date either. We've agreed to meet up to deal with something important!

After calming down, I decide to quickly resolve the dilemma in front of me. Under the pressure of Nadeshiko's scorching gaze, I lean over and speak into Ciri's ear to ask her for her opinion as a fellow person who is involved in the red-crowned crane incident.
{character:player}Can I roughly explain what we're doing to Nadeshiko?
{character:Ciri}Why are you so nervous if you haven't done anything wrong?
{character:player}Ahaha...
{character:Ciri}I get it. Tell her then, but I'm sure you know what you shouldn't tell her.
{character:Ciri}OK.
{character:player}OK.
I think Ciri is thinking of the same thing as me. There have been many hidden dangers in this red-crowned crane incident so far, so telling Nadeshiko everything might put her in danger too.
I think about what to say and then briefly explain the situation to Nadeshiko after omitting anything that might be dangerous.
{character:player}Actually, Ciri and I found an injured red-crowned crane the other day, and we've been busy trying to help it recently.
After I finish speaking and wait nervously for Nadeshiko's reply, Nadeshiko and Ciri suddenly burst out laughing.
{character:Nadeshiko}Haha, I told you right? Don't you think {var:player_nickname}'s embarrassed expression is cute?
{character:Ciri}Yeah, it is quite cute.
{character:player}Huh?
Nadeshiko turns to look and me and laughs while giving me an explanation.
{character:Nadeshiko}We couldn't resist teasing you since it's so fun to see you caught in a dilemma.
{character:Nadeshiko}Go and do what you need to do. I can always ask you to go on a ride with me next time.

After speaking, she stands up straight and holds her key tightly in her palm after twirling it around her finger twice. Nadeshiko shakes the jacket in her arms and puts it on, then she looks up at Ciri as if she has an afterthought.
{character:Nadeshiko}Shall we go out and have some fun together next time?
{character:Ciri}That sounds good. I kind of want to see whether my black panther or your "cheetah" has more explosive power.
{character:Nadeshiko}That's cheeky of you. Why don't we have a battle of endurance instead?
{character:Ciri}Then it'll forfeit, and I'll have to take its place instead.
{character:Nadeshiko}Haha, then let's talk about this later when I get to meet Mojito for real.
{character:Ciri}Sure.
{character:player}Sure.
Although I don't really understand their conversation, when I look behind Ciri... I feel sorry for Mojito who is being forced to participate in a race when it isn't even here.
After Nadeshiko leaves, Ciri and I make our way to the Raven hideout hastily. On our way there, I recall their conversation and ask Ciri a question curiously.
{character:player}What were you and Nadeshiko talking about earlier?
Ciri looks at me and smiles as she speaks.
{character:Ciri}Take a guess.
{character:player}Don't tell me you two are... going over the skeletons in my closet?
{character:Ciri}Take another guess.
This game is so hard.

As I get ready to regroup and try to pry more information from her, a serious expression appears on Ciri's face suddenly. I start to feel nervous immediately and quickly think about whether I did anything in front of Nadeshiko that would make Ciri furious.
Suddenly, Ciri pulls me behind her. After I turn around, I realize that a person in a clown costume is standing where I was just standing.

He appeared so quietly that I have no idea when he arrived or how long he has been here. Since Ciri's expression changed suddenly just now, I guess that this person must have arrived at that time, and Ciri's displeasure should be directed at this clown... I feel so relieved that she isn't angry about something in my past that I don't even know about.
The clown standing opposite us is wearing extremely exaggerated makeup, and the expression on his face is a smiling face with tears in his eyes. After bowing deeply to us, he hands over an envelope.

Instead of taking the envelope, Ciri stares at the clown silently. When the clown sees this, he makes a terrified expression and rubs the toes of his inward-facing feet together while looking at me uneasily from time to time.
Although I know he is acting, the conscious habit I had developed after taking action with Ciri these days makes me reflexively reach out and take the envelope.
The moment I take the envelope, the clown bursts into laughter and runs away, which makes me feel like he had given me a bomb and not an envelope...

As I have a deep trust in the peace and tranquility of One Han City, I open the envelope. Luckily, there's only a card inside. I take it out and inspect it, but all I can see is a clown's head on the back of the card and a line of words on the front side.
"Come to see me in the park if you want to know more about the organization that is behind the wildlife trafficking."
The name of the sender at the bottom is Ju.
{character:player}Who is this Ju?
Ciri takes the card from my hands and looks over it several times before sighing.
{character:Ciri}Do you still remember the clown mask you saw when you helped out at Soul in the past?
{character:player}Yeah, I remember it.
{character:Ciri}Ju is the owner of that mask. The clown that delivered the envelope should be one of his current companions.
{character:player}Is that the... traitor you mentioned in the past?
{character:player}If that's him, then could he have sent us this card because he knows what we are doing and wants to ruin our plans?
{character:Ciri}That shouldn't be the case. I think he really does know something. After all, I heard that he has managed to become connected with a certain government official.
{character:player}Do you think he'll tell us the truth?
{character:Ciri}He... probably will.
{character:Ciri}I don't actually have any personal grudges against him, but we just couldn't agree on what to do about Soul's crisis.

Although that's what she says, Ciri reached out for the whip at her waist subconsciously when she mentioned his name. When she notices the look in my eyes, Ciri snorts and gives me a further explanation with an unpleasant tone.

{character:Ciri}Although I don't have any personal grudges against him, he took most of the young members of Soul with him when he left, which is the direct reason for Soul's current lack of manpower.

{character:Ciri}Since you often come to watch our performances, you should know that Soul's logistical support is provided by a group of elderly people and children... No matter what, this reason alone is enough for me to never forgive him.

Ciri's words remind me of the physical condition of the elderly people in Soul who keep getting sick or injured, and that some of the jobs they are doing shouldn't be done by people their age... Someone should whip this Ju a couple of times.
But I also start hesitating when I look at the card in Ciri's hands. According to what Ciri said, it's very likely that Ju's information is true.
{character:player}Well... why don't we have a chat with Ju?
{character:Ciri}I refuse.

Ciri rejects my proposal straightforwardly and decisively, which doesn't surprise me at all. If I were in her shoes, it would also be difficult for me to bow down to a colleague who betrayed me in the past to get some information.

{character:player}Actually, what I've been thinking about is that although Soumu said he would give us an answer today, he didn't specify what answer he would give us. There's no guarantee that we'll be able to find the little red-crowned cranes.
{character:player}On the other hand, Ju claims that he has this information. I think this is a good opportunity, and we have nothing to lose either...
{character:Ciri}Hmm...
Seeing that Ciri is wavering, I decide to strike the iron while it's hot and give her another push.
{character:player}Besides, we still need to save the injured red-crowned crane and its two missing children. Since the opportunity to save them is in front of us, we shouldn't give up on it.
After thinking for a long time, Ciri is eventually convinced by me. She looks at me helplessly, and I can see traces of compromise in her usually determined eyes.
{character:Ciri}Sigh... Fine then. Let's go talk to Ju.
{character:player}For some reason, I feel like I've committed moral blackmail when I see you agree to my suggestion.

{character:Ciri}No, I think you're right. What I'm struggling with is my pride, whereas you're focusing on three living creatures. After everything we've been through in the last few days, I've realized that you're always able to notice many problems that I can't.
{character:Ciri}{var:player_nickname}, thank you.

Her sincerity makes me feel a little embarrassed. It's actually really easy to get along with someone like Ciri because she is very straightforward about who she likes and dislikes. And when she realizes that she's the one who's wrong, she will admit it readily without being coy about it. Also...
She is a terrific fighter, which makes her the best teammate in a mission!
Although Ju doesn't say which park he will be at, when I look at the map, I realize that there is only one park within 200 meters of our current location.

When Ciri and I arrive at the park, we aren't surprised to see the clown who delivered the envelope to us earlier at the entrance of the park. Above his head, his arms form a large heart shape in the air.
When Ciri ignores him completely and tries to walk right past him, the clown stops her and gestures for me to enter.
{character:player}So you want me to talk to Ju alone?

The clown makes a surprised expression and starts clapping while hopping on the ground. Even though he hasn't said a single word to us during this process, his rich and comical body language makes it easy for us to understand him.

Most of my previous knowledge about clowns comes from movies, television shows, and fast food restaurants. I'm starting to understand why this profession can bring laughter to children - their body language makes it easier for children to know what they are expressing and derive happiness from it.
After having a discussion with Ciri, I ask her to wait at the entrance while I enter the park alone.

The park is really small. After walking on the gravel path for a few minutes, a large lawn appears in front of me, and standing on the grass is a man wearing a red striped suit, a top hat of the same color, and clown makeup.

At this moment, he is leaning back vigorously like he is playing tug-of-war with an invisible opponent, and a group of children have gathered around him. Drawn in by his performance, the children keep shouting out and cheering for him like they are really watching an exciting tug-of-war contest.

Suddenly, the invisible rope seems to snap, and the clown falls backwards onto the ground from the inertia. After looking stunned for a moment, he suddenly makes a crying expression, and the children step forward to comfort him.

After being comforted by the children, the clown pushes the two corners of his mouth upwards with his index fingers and bends his eyes at the same time, instantly transforming his crying face into a smile.
I'm guessing that this person is Ju. Judging from his performance, he seems to be very skilled at making people happy. It's no wonder that he was such a popular performer of Soul at that time.

He also sees me at this time. He stands and motions for the children to calm down with his hands, then he takes off his top hat and rummages inside it seriously for a long time. Suddenly, his expression changes and he pulls his fist out of the top hat like he has found some treasure.

The children curiously step forward to try to pry open his fingers, but none of them succeed as they are too young and weak. The clown shakes his head at them before walking up to me, then he extends his clenched fist towards me.
I instantly understand his intentions and open his fingers one by one. In his palm is a candy wrapped in cellophane that looks bright and colorful in the sun.

After giving me the candy, the clown takes out lots of candies from the pockets of his clothes and distributes them to the children around us. He then waves to the children and asks them to take the candies and leave us for a while.
When there is no one around us, the clown makes a gentlemanly salute and introduces himself.
{character:???}This weather is perfect for a chance encounter, don't you think? I'm Ju, a clown of Gemini.
{character:player}Hi, I'm {var:player_nickname}, Ciri's friend.
Ju
{character:Ju}No, no, no, you're wrong.
{character:Ju}You're her close friend. Ciri and I have known each other for many years, and this is the first time I've seen her hanging out with a living person and not her group of animal friends.
{character:player}Since you've known each other for so long, why won't you let her come here?
{character:Ju}I don't think you want this clean grass to be dyed red, do you?
I understand what he is saying. Ciri will definitely get into an argument with him, so it's more appropriate for me to pass on messages for them as an intermediary.
{character:Ju}I have a question to ask you before I tell you the information you want.
{character:player}What is it?
{character:Ju}Are you really going to get involved in Soul's matters? I can probably guess why you've been taking action with Ciri.
{character:player}It looks like you still care about Soul.
Ju doesn't refute me. Instead, he pushes the two corners of his mouth upwards with his index fingers into a smile again, but I get the feeling that he isn't really smiling this time.
{character:Ju}Soul's future is a bottomless pit. You won't have the unlimited energy required to keep it afloat.
{character:player}Why do you say that?
Ju takes a pen and a card from the inner pocket of his jacket. It looks like the same one he used to deliver the message to us earlier. He keeps talking to me while he writes and draws on the card.
{character:Ju}Let's play a fun game.

{character:Ju}You're a train conductor who is driving a train to the city next door that is still under construction. On the train is a group of young people with a bright future. They are the builders of the city next door, and they are talking about their ideals on the train.
{character:Ju}Suddenly, as you are about to arrive at a fork, you see a strong worker tied to the left tracks and five old people tied to the right tracks.

{character:Ju}It is already known that this fast-moving train can't stop anywhere other than at a station or else it'll derail due to the inertia. If that happens, the train will crash with a massive boom, and everyone on it will die.
{character:Ju}Fortunately, you still have a choice. There's a lever in front of you, which controls whether the train moves to the left or the right.

After saying this, he shows me the card in his hand. On it is a very abstract drawing, and I can tell that it is a train that is moving towards a fork. There are stick figures lying on the tracks on both sides of the train after the fork.
Ju holds this card up in the air for me to see with one hand. The palm of his other hand is facing me, and his five fingers are spread open.
{character:Ju}I'll now count to five. After that, you need to tell me if the train should move to the left or the right.
The trolley problem is an ethical topic that people often discuss, but now that someone has asked me to answer this question, I start considering it seriously instead of joking like usual.
The reason for this is because Ju isn't really presenting me with a trolley problem, but the story of Soul and him.
I'm not quite sure what deeper meaning this question has from Ju's point of view, but from my point of view, making the train move to the left will result in the smallest amount of loss.
{character:player}I'll make the train move to the left... it looks like this will result in the smallest amount of loss.
{character:Ju}To the left... Let's see what will happen if it moves to the left.

{character:Ju}You've chosen to sacrifice the strong worker. You arrive at a station soon after passing through the fork. When you stop there, you save the five old people and continue your journey with them on the train.
{character:Ju}As there are suddenly five extra people, your supplies, which were originally just enough for everyone, are no longer sufficient.

{character:Ju}At first, everyone is willing to give them a portion of their own supplies, but as time passes by, they gradually discover that these five people have no ability to work. They can't provide any help to anyone, and they use the moral standard of respecting the elderly to coerce everyone into serving them.

{character:Ju}As the elderly consume medical supplies many times faster than normal young people, the medical supplies of the train are soon stretched thin. The shortage of supplies caused conflicts to arise. The young people no longer talked about their ideals, but instead start to constantly argue for survival...
{character:Ju}This continues until one of the old people disappears one day. They find pieces of his clothing on the train door, and someone suddenly whispers something...
{character:Ju}"When I got up to go to the toilet last night, I think I saw someone push him off the speeding train."

{character:Ju}Everyone seems to hear this. Over the next few days, the second, third, fourth, and then the last elderly person disappears. The train then resumes its former peace, as if nothing had happened.
As he says this, he moves closer to me and whispers in my ear.
{character:Ju}Is this really the decision that will result in the smallest amount of loss?
The story doesn't unfold as I expected, so I fall deep in thought for a moment.
{character:player}You... What choice did you make?
{character:Ju}Me? Haha, of course I chose to move to the right. This way, everyone has a bright future. Isn't that great? Also...
{character:Ju}In essence, there is no difference between sacrificing one person and sacrificing five people. You're still an executioner. The only difference is which sacrifice is more meaningful.
{character:player}Hmm... So you chose to move to the right to save the train called Soul and not the worker. Am I right?
{character:Ju}Yes.
Ju's reason for betraying Soul isn't what I expected. Or rather, if this is why he left Soul, then it can't even be called a betrayal.
{character:player}Why...
{character:Ju}Shush--
He interrupts my question by motioning for me to be quiet.
{character:Ju}If you've chosen to side with Sara, then you shouldn't ask me, a traitor, your next question.
{character:Ju}But since you played a game with me earnestly, I should respond to you in kind. This is what you want.
As he speaks, Ju takes another envelope from his inside pocket and hands it to me. It's almost as if a blue robotic cat's dimensional pocket is hidden under his plain-looking jacket.
{character:Ju}This is a welcome gift from a fellow "executioner." I hope you'll choose to make a more meaningful sacrifice one day.

On the train is a group of young people with a bright future and hopes of building a city, and on the left track is a worker that can create value. When viewed purely from the perspective of benefits, it is most cost-effective to sacrifice these five old people, even if this idea is very selfish and extreme... After all, these five old people might also have created value when they were young.
It's not a nice feeling to be an executioner, but as a decision-maker, you need to take responsibility for your own ideas and the future of the people who follow you.
{character:player}I choose to move to the right.
Clap--Clap--Clap-- Ju starts clapping after hearing my answer.
{character:Ju}Well, let's see what happens after you choose to make the train move to the right.

{character:Ju}You've chosen to sacrifice the five old people. You arrive at a station soon after passing through the fork. When you stop there, you save the worker and continue your journey with him on the train.

{character:Ju}Although there's now one extra person on the train, everyone only needs to share a small portion of their supplies with him to keep him alive. Out of gratitude to everyone, the worker works very hard, which improves everyone's opinion of him.

{character:Ju}It's inevitable that various problems will arise on such a long train ride. While performing an emergency repair one time, the worker showed amazing maintenance skills, and everyone discovered that he was a skilled maintenance worker who was best at dealing with machinery.

{character:Ju}Under the maintenance of the worker, although it's a stretch to say that the train has been refreshed, its service life has indeed been significantly extended. As a result, everyone's belief that they will be able to smoothly reach their ideal city becomes firmer, and the train continues to move forward, carrying everyone's hopes with it.
I don't ask him out loud, but I know this is what Ju chose to do back then.
After telling me this story, Ju takes another envelope from his inside pocket and hands it to me. It's almost as if a blue robotic cat's dimensional pocket is hidden under his plain-looking jacket.
I can't make the decision to sacrifice the five old people or the young worker. I don't say anything after the countdown ends.
{character:Ju}It looks like you can't make a decision. Well, let's see what happens next.

{character:Ju}Because you aren't able to choose which way to pull the lever in time, the train derails due to inertia... You soon hear the sound of wailing, explosions, items breaking, and liquid spraying all around you.

{character:Ju}Most of the young people on the train lose their lives before they can even see the city they plan to build. Even if someone is lucky enough to survive, they no longer trust you as the train conductor because of this incident and choose to leave.
{character:Ju}At this time, you remember that there are six people who survived because of your mercy. When you run over to untie them and set them free, you find that...

{character:Ju}They aren't at all grateful to you about the train not running over them. Instead, they think the accident is caused by an error in your judgment and believe that maybe no one would have died if you did your job as the train conductor properly.

{character:Ju}See? A person who can't even take care of their own train is ridiculously trying to save everyone. This is clearly unrealistic. All these signs prove that you... are not meant to be a decision-maker.
{character:Ju}You made the same decision that Sara made that year.
Since he said that I "made the same decision that Sara made that year," it must mean that they faced the same problem back then. In that case...
{character:player}What choice did you make?
{character:Ju}Me? Haha, of course I chose to move to the right. This way, everyone has a bright future. Isn't that great?
{character:player}I don't know the model answer to this question, but I know it isn't right to choose the left or the right.
{character:player}We can't actively hurt others just because our own interests are threatened. No one has the right to decide the fate of others.

{character:Ju}Haha, aren't the interests of the young people on the train important? Because of your hesitation, they have lost their lives, dreams, and futures. Haven't you also unilaterally decided their fate?
{character:player}I haven't given up on them. Although trying to save everyone looks unrealistic, that alone shouldn't stop us from aiming to achieve this objective.

{character:player}There are many things we can do before the train hits the track and derails, such as slowing down the train, trying to stop it, asking for help, or getting others to save the people on the tracks... We can always find a glimmer of opportunity.
{character:player}It's too cruel to give up on someone else's life without trying to do anything.
{character:Ju}Opportunity... Opportunity? Hahahahaha...

Ju starts laughing to himself like he has heard something really funny. His shoulders keep moving up and down, and he soon bends over and puts his hands on his knees to support himself as he laughs loudly and uncontrollably.
After a while, he stands and rubs his eyes with his hands before he looks at me.
{character:Ju}You're too funny. You made me laugh so hard I started crying.
{character:Ju}Well, do you think you're Soul's opportunity?
{character:player}I... I don't know, but I'm willing to try my best.

Clap--Clap--Clap-- He claps three times crisply, then pulls out another envelope from his inside pocket as an afterthought and hands it to me. It's almost as if a blue robotic cat's dimensional pocket is hidden under his plain-looking jacket.
{character:Ju}I can't wait to see what opportunities you'll bring to Soul then.
{character:Ciri}Since Ju has told you the general situation of what happened back then, I'll tell you the whole story so you don't have any wild thoughts.

{character:Ciri}Ju and I were both adopted by Sid, the second-generation leader of Soul when we were children. Unlike Sara, who grew up in a rich family and joined Soul because she loved dancing, we had been touring everywhere with the troupe since we were young, and we were used to the fickleness of human nature.

{character:Ciri}Sid and Sara were both born into wealthy families and received similar educations since they were young, so they had a similar outlook on things. That's why Sid chose Sara to be the third-generation leader of Soul instead of Ju, who had always been working hard to become Sid's successor. In his eyes, Sid was favoring Sara over him.

{character:Ciri}As you know, Soul used to travel throughout the world when performing on tour, and the group has had a practice of taking in people who had no home to return to since the first-generation leader led the group. After spending so much time together, we became more like family than colleagues.

{character:Ciri}This kind of relationship has both advantages and disadvantages. One disadvantage is that Soul now has a large number of old, feeble, sick, and sometimes disabled people who contribute little to the group, which has made our finances increasingly tight... By the time Sara took over as leader, we were already struggling to make ends meet, and we mostly performed to make a living.

{character:Ciri}Ju noticed this problem a long time ago. He believed that it would be better to deal with the problem once and for all no matter how painful it would be rather than prolong the agony. Instead of letting these people become a burden to Soul, he wanted to make them leave Soul and find their own way to survive.

{character:Ciri}Sara regards Soul as her home, and the members as her family. She believed that only they themselves could decide whether they would leave or stay, and not even the leader could make that decision for them.
{character:player}What about you?
{character:Ciri}Me?
{character:player}Didn't you want to become the leader?
{character:Ciri}I'm used to being a loner. The position of leader is a burden to me.
{character:player}What do you think about Ju and Sara's disagreement?

{character:Ciri}Actually, wild beasts often choose to abandon the old, feeble, sick, and disabled to preserve the rest of the population. This isn't anything strange in nature, so I won't judge whether Ju or Sara is right or wrong. They are both trying to protect Soul in different ways, and even I have my own way of protecting Soul.
{character:Ciri}I have chosen to stay with Sara because my intuition tells me that Sara is able to give Soul a brighter future.

{character:Ciri}Okay, that's the end of the story. {var:player_nickname}, you've always been a person who has strong opinions, so I won't ask you to side with any of us. You just need to continue doing what you think is right.
{character:player}Hmm, yeah.

Neither Ciri nor I pursue this topic further. Instead, we open the envelope Ju gave me after a moment of silence and find a hand-drawn map inside it. Based on the feeling of familiarity I get from this soul painting, I believe Ju drew this himself.
As the street name is marked, it's easy to tell that the destination is a club in the east side of the city. In fact, it's only a few streets away from the Raven hideout we visited yesterday.
Ciri and I exchange a glance and decide to show Soumu this map.

By the time we arrive at the Raven hideout, it is already well past the time we agreed to meet Soumu. On the way there, my quick-witted brain works furiously to think of an explanation for our lateness.
After thinking about it, I decide that the best solution is to show him the map and tell him we've found a suspicious place.

However, the scene in front of the hideout is not what I expected at all. There are two groups of people confronting each other on both sides of the street, and the tension is so thick that no pedestrians dare to pass through them.
Fortunately, this street isn't a main road, or else each person would be fined 5,000 Coppers for obstructing traffic.

Shijukara sees us from a distance and quickly calls for us to go over to him and stand behind Soumu together. Speaking in a low voice, I ask him what is going on while Ciri stares at the other side with a serious look on her face.
{character:player}What's going on?
Shijukara

{character:Shijukara}The people standing opposite us are from Strix based in the west side of the city, and they've always been at odds with us. They are just a gang of barbaric information dealers though, so you don't need to be scared.
{character:player}Why have they come here today? Are they here to fight you? Is this a gang fight?
{character:player}Did your boss accept?
{character:Shijukara}Of course not. That's why we're all stuck here.
{character:player}Oh, so even you know that the situation is very tense.
{character:Shijukara}Nonsense! I'm not stupid.
If this is the reason... I think for a moment, then I take the map out of my pocket and hand it to Soumu.
{character:player}Aniki, please take a look at this. I've found a suspicious location.
I didn't really expect that this excuse would come in handy. I'm so smart.
The young man wearing a hat at the very front of the people across the street looks at me with interest and suddenly starts speaking.
{character:???}{var:player_nickname}.
